AND AWARD DATED 11.11.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO. 1218/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, MACT-IV,
CHITRADURGA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,64,891/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries :
i. Swelling, tenderness, restricted movement present in the right elbow joint;
ii. Multiple abrasions present over the left knee joint and right foot; and iii. Fracture of proximal 1/3rd of ulna with dislocation of radial head, postinary of right elbow.
4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:

2. Medical expenditure 67,291 3.

4. Loss of amenities 10,000/-

5.
The Tribunal has, while awarding the said sum has assessed the disability of the claimant to the whole body at 8% and has taken the notional income at Rs.9,000/- per month.

In my view, the assessment of disability at 8% to the whole body cannot be found fault with since the Doctor who had examined the claimant stated that the claimant had suffered the disability at 32% to the upper limb.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.9,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year, would be Rs.11,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 40 years, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,58,400 (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x '15' x 8%) towards 'loss of future income' .
8. The evidence on record indicates that the claimant was hospitalised for eight days.

In this view of the matter, a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.10,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' deserves to be enhanced and accordingly it is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- and Rs.30,000/-
respectively.
9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards 'food and nourishment'.
In my view, it would be appropriate that the said sum be enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.

10. The Tribunal has determined the laid-up period as two months and having regard to the fact that the claimant has suffered 32% disability to the upper limb, it would be appropriate to determine the laid-up period as four months and award a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the said head.
11.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards 'removal of implants' and Rs.67,291/-
towards 'medical expenditure', in my view the said sum is just and proper and is affirmed.

Similarly,
Rs.10,000/- awarded towards 'attendant charges' is affirmed.
12. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
